name: fig-09
title: fig-09: Growth & division
question: Does the paper's §Growth-and-division claim (Fig. division) hold as a runnable composite -- that division is a compositional rewrite in which "one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores partitioned across daughters and interface ports duplicated" (caption a: DNA replication, elongation, septum, separation; caption b: "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA and biomass into two cells") -- when realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store driven through the process-bigraph engine?
biological_summary:
This is the executable realization of the paper's §Growth, division, development, evolution section and its Fig. division. The paper frames division as the more radical of the transformations a self-maintaining cellular interface undergoes: "a compositional rewrite in which one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores $x$ partitioned across daughters and interface ports $W$ duplicated and re-established" -- each daughter inheriting a subset of stores and reconstructing a viable interface. Caption a walks the prokaryotic sequence (DNA replication, elongation, septum formation, separation into daughters); caption b abstracts it to "a compositional rewrite that partitions state variables such as DNA and biomass into two cells."

The `fig09-rewrite` composite (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.fig09-rewrite`, built via `build_fig10_division`) realizes exactly caption b at the place-graph level. A single `CellCycleDivision` Process owns a colony `tree[node]` store holding one founder cell, itself holding one chromosome carrying `dna = 1.0`. Every `cycle` (= 3) time units the process alternates two genuine place-graph rewrites, emitted as an `overwrite[tree[node]]` so removed nodes actually disappear from the trajectory:

REPLICATE -- a cell holding one chromosome duplicates it into two sisters (the DNA-copy step; the total DNA store doubles while the boundary count stays 1). DIVIDE -- a cell holding two sisters splits into two daughter cells with fresh ids, partitioning one chromosome to each (the boundary rewrite: one node becomes two, each daughter's cell subtree re-established with its own chromosome port). Because both rewrites apply to every cell each round, running it forward keeps dividing: 1 -> 2 -> 4 cells over the default 12-tick run, replication always preceding division.

This is a DIDACTIC, toy-real composite: the "growth" that drives division here is discrete DNA replication reaching two chromosomes (the division precondition), NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold, and the cycle length, DNA amounts, and capacity cap are illustrative model units, not fitted to any organism's replication timing or genome size. Its purpose is to make the paper's "division is a compositional rewrite" claim literally executable and steppable frame by frame -- one boundary becoming two at runtime -- not to reproduce quantitative division kinetics. The rigorous spatial cousin, where a real CPM cell grows and divides with per-pixel biomass, is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

The composite is a pure clock-driven rewrite with NO randomness, so the whole trajectory is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run: founder 1 cell / dna 1.0; at t=3 replication gives 1 cell / 2 chromosomes / dna 2.0; at t=6 division gives 2 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 2.0); at t=9 replication gives 2 cells / 4 chromosomes / dna 4.0; at t=12 division gives 4 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 4.0). The caption-b claim -- division partitions the DNA store into two daughters, conserving it -- is asserted directly from the emitted trajectory: at every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, total DNA is unchanged across the split, and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA.
claim: Realizing the paper's Fig. division caption b as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store (one `CellCycleDivision` process alternating REPLICATE and DIVIDE rewrites, driven through the process-bigraph engine) reproduces "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells": over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell replicates its chromosome (DNA store doubles 1.0 -> 2.0 while the boundary count stays 1) then divides (one cell becomes two, each daughter carrying one chromosome with dna 1.0), and repeats to 4 cells -- and at every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (2.0 -> 2x1.0; 4.0 -> 4x1.0, nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA. Replication always precedes division. This is a toy-real, uncalibrated didactic composite -- the division trigger is a discrete cell-cycle clock reaching a replicated (two-chromosome) state, not an integrated biomass threshold -- whose point is to make "division is a compositional rewrite" literally executable, not to reproduce division kinetics.

variants.name: fig09-mechanistic
variants.rationale: Real-mechanism upgrade (scientific-review revision, Oct 2026). The baseline fig09-rewrite divides on a fixed clock and the duplicated chromosome's DNA appears from nowhere — verifying the place-graph rewrite + equipartition (bookkeeping) but not biological growth or a self-sustaining cycle. This variant (GrowthDivisionColony) makes division an OUTCOME of physiology on the same colony tree[node]: each cell GROWS by Michaelis–Menten uptake of a shared, finite nutrient; REPLICATES only past a size checkpoint and with the nucleotides+energy for it, drawing the new chromosome's DNA FROM a nucleotide precursor pool (DNA+nucleotides conserved — no DNA from nothing); and DIVIDES only when volume ≥ V_div AND replicated AND energy ≥ div_cost, partitioning volume/energy/nucleotides/biomass/chromosomes between two daughters that continue. Starve the nutrient and division is DELAYED, not clocked. Baseline kept intact as the didactic smoke test.

key_assumptions: This `fig09-rewrite` composite is DIDACTIC / toy-real: a small, illustrative place-graph rewrite built to look like Fig. division and play forward, NOT calibrated to any organism. The cycle length (3 time units), the per-chromosome DNA amount (1.0), the capacity cap (16 cells), and the run length (12 ticks) are illustrative model units chosen to make replicate -> divide -> repeat legible, not fitted to real replication timing, genome size, or growth rate.

The "growth" that gates division here is DISCRETE DNA replication -- a cell reaching two chromosomes is the division precondition -- driven by a cell-cycle clock, NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold. The paper's caption b names "DNA and biomass"; this composite realizes the DNA-partition half literally (chromosomes with a `dna` store) and treats division timing as clock-driven rather than biomass-threshold-driven.

Division is realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite: the process returns an `overwrite[tree[node]]`, deleting the parent cell node and adding two fresh daughter cell nodes each with its own chromosome subtree -- so "interface ports duplicated" is realized as each daughter re-establishing a cell->chromosome place-graph structure, NOT as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment (this composite has no environment/metabolism coupling at all).

The composite is fully deterministic: there is no randomness anywhere in `CellCycleDivision` (a clock plus structural rewrites), so every count and DNA value in this study is an exact, run-to-run-reproducible pin, not a representative single-run value.

The rigorous cousin `growth-and-division` (in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation) realizes growth-then-division with a real CPM cell and per-pixel biomass; this study does NOT restate that cousin's numbers. This study's contribution is the compositional-rewrite / store-partition principle at the place-graph level, made executable and steppable.
acceptance_criteria: Over the run the colony''s cell count increases from one founder to at least four cells, and is never decreasing -- cells are only ADDED by division, never removed.
Replication precedes division -- the chromosome (DNA) count doubles while the cell count is still one, before any cell has partitioned that DNA into daughters.
The total DNA store doubles at each replication event (1.0 -> 2.0 -> 4.0), realizing the DNA-copy step of caption a.

At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is CONSERVED across the rewrite (sum over daughters equals the pre-division total; nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly HALF of a parent cell''s DNA -- caption b''s "partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells."

units_and_time.time: 1 tick = 1 dimensionless model time unit; the run is 12 ticks with a cell cycle of 3, so replication/division events fall at t = 3, 6, 9, 12.
units_and_time.quantities: cell and chromosome counts are integer node counts in the colony place graph; the `dna` store is a dimensionless model quantity (founder chromosome carries dna = 1.0), NOT a calibrated genome mass. The capacity cap (16 cells) is a finite-tree guard, not a biological carrying capacity.
units_and_time.note: No quantity here is calibrated to a named organism, replication rate, or genome size -- all magnitudes are toy-real, chosen for didactic legibility.

findings.statement: Division realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite ADDS cell nodes at runtime and orders replication before division, exactly as caption a describes (DNA replication then separation into daughters). Over a deterministic 12-tick run the colony grows 1 -> 2 -> 4 cells, the count never falling, and at each round the chromosome count doubles (replication) a half-cycle before the cell count doubles (division). Confirmed: cells reach 4, monotone non-decreasing; first replication at t=3 strictly precedes first division at t=6.

evidence.observed: cells 1 -> 2 (t=6) -> 4 (t=12); chromosome count doubles at t=3 while cells still 1

findings.statement: The composite realizes caption b's core claim -- "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells" -- as a CONSERVING, EQUIPARTITIONING rewrite. At each replication the total DNA store doubles (1.0 -> 2.0 -> 4.0); at each division the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA is conserved across the split (nothing created or destroyed), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA. Confirmed at both division events: t=6 (2.0 conserved, 1.0 per daughter) and t=12 (4.0 conserved, 1.0 per daughter). One maintained boundary becomes two with its stores partitioned across the daughters -- executable, not merely drawn.

evidence.observed: division events: 1->2 cells, DNA 2.0 conserved -> 1.0 each; 2->4 cells, DNA 4.0 conserved -> 1.0 each (each daughter = half of parent, all deterministic)

findings.statement: The per-cell DNA content follows a strict replicate-then-halve invariant across the whole cell cycle, sharper than the aggregate conservation claim. Over the deterministic 12-tick run the per-cell DNA vector cycles [1.0] -> [2.0] -> [1.0, 1.0] -> [2.0, 2.0] -> [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]: each cell doubles its chromosome to dna 2.0 at replication, then splits into two daughters of exactly dna 1.0 at division. So immediately after each division every cell carries exactly one chromosome at the 1.0 founder set point and the total DNA store exactly equals the cell count -- the "one chromosome, dna == 1.0 per daughter" invariant holds identically at both division events. Confirmed in-memory via build_fig10_division(cycle=3).

evidence.observed: per-cell DNA by tick: t=0 [1.0]; t=3 [2.0]; t=6 [1.0, 1.0]; t=9 [2.0, 2.0]; t=12 [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0] -- total DNA == cell count at every post-division state

findings.statement: Division becomes an OUTCOME of physiology, not a clock — fixing the review's objection that the baseline's 1→2→4 verifies only the graph rewrite. In the mechanistic variant each cell grows by Michaelis–Menten uptake of a shared finite nutrient and divides ONLY when it has grown past a size checkpoint, completed replication, and has the energy for it. The colony grows 1→2→4→8→16 when fed, but under starvation (nutrient ≈ 0) the cell never reaches the checkpoint and division is DELAYED indefinitely (0 divisions over 40 ticks). A grown but under-energised or un-replicated cell also does not divide. So the 1→2→4→8→16 is now caused by growth, with the inter-division interval set by how fast the cell grows.

evidence.observed: full 1→16 over 20 ticks; starved stays 1 (0 divisions / 40 ticks); no division without energy or replication

findings.statement: DNA replication is now mass-accounted, and every material partition is conserved across the rewrite. The duplicated chromosome's DNA is drawn FROM a nucleotide precursor pool (Δ DNA = −Δ nucleotides to <1e-9), so DNA is not created from nothing — the review's "account for nucleotides" point. At division, volume, nucleotides, biomass and DNA sum over the two daughters exactly equals the parent's, energy equals the parent's minus the one-time division cost, and each daughter inherits exactly one chromosome of equal DNA as a distinct lineage node. The baseline's exact 1→2→4 equipartition is preserved, now on top of genuine growth and nucleotide bookkeeping.

evidence.observed: Δ(DNA) == −Δ(nucleotides) <1e-9 per replication; all partitions conserved <1e-9; energy = parent − div_cost

findings.statement: Honest scope. The mechanistic variant demonstrates that division can be gated by growth/energy/size with conserved, nucleotide-accounted replication over a lineage — but it is still a reduced model: growth is a single lumped Michaelis–Menten uptake (no explicit metabolic network), the checkpoints are hand-set volume/energy thresholds (not a modelled regulatory circuit), partition is exactly symmetric (no stochastic asymmetry or timing variability), and there is no spatial constriction geometry. The baseline's exact 1→2→4 + DNA equipartition remains bookkeeping verification; the upgrade is that the TIMING and OCCURRENCE of division are now caused by physiology. The rigorous spatial cousin (a CPM cell growing by per-pixel biomass and dividing spatially) is `growth-and-division` in draft-to-living-cell.

evidence.observed: gated, conserved, nucleotide-accounted division over a 16-cell lineage; symmetric deterministic partition

regression_compatibility.basis: fig09-rewrite.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the process-bigraph engine over a deterministic 12-tick run (tests/test_fig09_dynamics.py); the RAMEmitter captures the full colony subtree each tick so runtime-added place-graph nodes appear in the trajectory.

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig09-rewrite): the colony grows 1→2→4, replication precedes division, total DNA doubles at replication, and every division doubles the boundary count while conserving + equipartitioning the DNA store — all exact deterministic pins. This verifies the place-graph REWRITE and bookkeeping, not biological growth (division fires on a clock; the duplicated DNA appears for free). MECHANISTIC (variant fig09-mechanistic): division is an OUTCOME of growth/energy/size (starvation delays it indefinitely; a mechanistic_ablation), replication draws DNA from a nucleotide pool so DNA+nucleotides is conserved (invariant), and every material partition is conserved across the rewrite with energy = parent − div_cost. This is genuine mechanistic support for "division is a compositional rewrite driven by growth." NOT yet empirical validation against a measured cell-cycle time, growth rate, or genome — that remains the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell`.

explanatory_gain.basis: Realizing Fig. division as a genuine `overwrite[tree[node]]` rewrite -- deleting one cell node and adding two daughter nodes with partitioned chromosome subtrees at runtime -- makes the paper's "division is a compositional rewrite in which one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores partitioned across daughters" claim literally executable and steppable, rather than a static three-panel drawing. A viewer can watch one boundary become two and the DNA store split evenly, frame by frame.

conclusion:
## Claims

- Realizing the paper's Fig. division caption b as a genuine place-graph rewrite over a colony `tree[node]` store (one `CellCycleDivision` process alternating REPLICATE and DIVIDE rewrites through the process-bigraph engine) reproduces "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells." Over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell replicates its chromosome (DNA store 1.0 -> 2.0, boundary count still 1) then divides (one cell becomes two, each daughter carrying one chromosome with dna 1.0), repeating to 4 cells.

- At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite (2.0 -> 2x1.0; 4.0 -> 4x1.0), and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA -- caption b's store-partition claim, asserted directly from the emitted trajectory. Replication always precedes division (caption a's replicate-then-separate ordering).

## Evidence

- **CELL-COUNT-INCREASES-DIVISION-HAPPENED** -- cells 1 (t=0-5) -> 2 (t=6-11) -> 4 (t=12), monotone non-decreasing

- **REPLICATION-PRECEDES-DIVISION** -- chromosome count doubles at t=3 (cells still 1); cells first double at t=6

- **TOTAL-DNA-DOUBLES-AT-REPLICATION** -- total DNA 1.0 -> 2.0 (t=3) -> 4.0 (t=9)

- **DIVISION-CONSERVES-AND-EQUIPARTITIONS-DNA** -- t=6 (1->2, DNA 2.0 conserved, 1.0 each) and t=12 (2->4, DNA 4.0 conserved, 1.0 each); boundary count doubles, each daughter = half of parent

## Limitations

- Didactic / toy-real: cycle length, DNA amounts, capacity cap, and run length are illustrative model units, not calibrated to any organism's replication timing or genome size.

- The division trigger is a discrete cell-cycle clock reaching a replicated (two-chromosome) state, NOT an integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold; the caption's "biomass" half is not modeled as a continuous store here.

- "Interface ports duplicated" is realized as each daughter re-establishing a cell->chromosome place-graph subtree, not as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment -- this composite has no environment/metabolism coupling.

- The rigorous spatial cousin is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation (a real CPM cell growing and dividing with per-pixel biomass); this study does not restate its numbers.

## Next steps

- Couple a continuous biomass store that integrates to a division threshold, so division timing is emergent rather than clock-driven.

- Add an environment coupling so daughters must re-establish interface fluxes after division, realizing the "interface ports ... re-established" half of the paper's claim quantitatively.

But it remains a REDUCED model: growth is a single lumped Michaelis–Menten uptake (no explicit metabolic network or ATP/biomass stoichiometry), the V_rep/V_div/energy checkpoints are hand-set thresholds (not a modelled cell-cycle regulatory circuit), partition is exactly symmetric and deterministic (no stochastic timing or asymmetric division), and there is no spatial constriction/septum geometry. Not calibrated to any organism's cell-cycle time, growth rate, or genome size. The rigorous spatial cousin is `growth-and-division` in draft-to-living-cell.

Didactic / toy-real composite: the cell-cycle length (3), per-chromosome DNA (1.0), capacity cap (16), and 12-tick run are illustrative model units chosen for legibility, not calibrated to any organism's replication timing, growth rate, or genome size.

The "growth" that gates division is DISCRETE DNA replication reaching two chromosomes (a cell-cycle clock precondition), NOT a continuously integrated biomass store crossing a calibrated threshold. The caption names "DNA and biomass"; this composite realizes the DNA-partition half literally and treats division timing as clock-driven, leaving continuous biomass growth to the spatial cousin.

"Interface ports duplicated and re-established" is realized structurally -- each daughter re-establishes a cell->chromosome place-graph subtree -- not as re-wiring quantitative interface fluxes to an environment. This composite has no environment/metabolism coupling at all, so daughters do not have to re-couple to nutrients to remain viable.

This study demonstrates the compositional-rewrite / store-partition PRINCIPLE at the place-graph level and does NOT restate the cousin's calibrated numbers as its own.
falsifiability: Overturned if the colony fails to grow from one founder to at least four cells, if the cell count ever decreases (division removing rather than adding boundaries), if division precedes replication in any round, if the total DNA store fails to double at a replication event, if total DNA is not conserved across a division event (mass created or destroyed in the split), or if any division fails to partition the parent's DNA evenly (a daughter dropped or the split uneven) -- any of which would break the "division partitions state variables such as DNA into two cells" claim. Because the composite is deterministic, any such failure would reproduce exactly.

experiment: Run the `fig09-rewrite` composite (`CellCycleDivision` over a colony `tree[node]` store, cycle=3, built via build_fig10_division) to completion over 12 ticks through the process-bigraph engine, capturing the whole colony subtree each tick, and measure whether a genuine place-graph rewrite realizes the paper's Fig. division caption b -- whether the boundary count doubles at each division while the DNA store is copied at replication and then conserved and equipartitioned across each division.
result: Over a deterministic 12-tick run the founder cell (1 cell, dna 1.0) replicates its chromosome at t=3 (1 cell, 2 chromosomes, dna 2.0), then divides at t=6 into 2 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 2.0), replicates again at t=9 (2 cells, 4 chromosomes, dna 4.0), and divides at t=12 into 4 cells with dna 1.0 each (total conserved at 4.0). At every division event the boundary count exactly doubles, the total DNA store is conserved across the rewrite, and each daughter inherits exactly half of a parent cell's DNA -- caption b's "division ... partitions state variables such as DNA ... into two cells." Replication always precedes division (caption a's replicate-then-separate ordering). Every value is an exact, run-to-run-reproducible pin because the composite has no randomness. This is a toy-real, uncalibrated didactic realization whose point is to make "division is a compositional rewrite" literally executable at the place-graph level -- one boundary becoming two, its stores partitioned across daughters, steppable frame by frame -- not to reproduce division kinetics; the rigorous spatial cousin is `growth-and-division` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig09-rewrite): the colony grows 1→2→4, replication precedes division, total DNA doubles at replication, and every division doubles the boundary count while conserving + equipartitioning the DNA store — all exact deterministic pins. This verifies the place-graph REWRITE and bookkeeping, not biological growth (division fires on a clock; the duplicated DNA appears for free). MECHANISTIC (variant fig09-mechanistic): division is an OUTCOME of growth/energy/size (starvation delays it indefinitely; a mechanistic_ablation), replication draws DNA from a nucleotide pool so DNA+nucleotides is conserved (invariant), and every material partition is conserved across the rewrite with energy = parent − div_cost. This is genuine mechanistic support for "division is a compositional rewrite driven by growth." NOT yet empirical validation against a measured cell-cycle time, growth rate, or genome — that remains the sibling investigation `draft-to-living-cell`.

explanatory_gain.basis: Realizing Fig. division as a genuine `overwrite[tree[node]]` rewrite -- deleting one cell node and adding two daughter nodes with partitioned chromosome subtrees at runtime -- makes the paper's "division is a compositional rewrite in which one maintained boundary becomes two, with stores partitioned across daughters" claim literally executable and steppable, rather than a static three-panel drawing. A viewer can watch one boundary become two and the DNA store split evenly, frame by frame.

derived.insight: Division realized as a genuine place-graph rewrite ADDS cell nodes at runtime and orders replication before division, exactly as caption a describes (DNA replication then separation into daughters). Over a deterministic 12-tick run the colony grows 1 -> 2 -> 4 cells, the count never falling, and at each round the chromosome count doubles (replication) a half-cycle before the cell count doubles (division). Confirmed: cells reach 4, monotone non-decreasing; first replication at t=3 strictly precedes first division at t=6.
